title: The Frost Line
lead: The Vesper Landing's heat plant died an hour ago with eleven hundred people aboard, and you can lift off half of them before the cold gets there. Then a Hegemony cutter drops out of nowhere with its lights on, and a very polite Inspector Moor asks if she can be of any assistance.
anyone: The Vesper Landing's heat plant has died with eleven hundred people aboard, and there aren't shuttles enough to lift them off before the cold gets there. Then a Hegemony cutter drops out of nowhere with its lights on, and a very polite Inspector Moor asks if she can be of any assistance.

gm.truth: The heat plant failed because its spare coil was requisitioned three weeks ago for the Meridian's drive. The form has the captain's signature, in a stack of a hundred such forms. Inspector Jaska Moor has a copy, and shows it, politely. The frost line moves a deck every forty minutes. Moor has a cutter and a big Hegemony transport one short jump behind it, and she can lift everyone in an hour. She means it. Each adult just has to sign a five-year Bastion Nine service contract first, with families kept together. It's the same nine hundred pages, and nobody reads page 614 while they're freezing. She isn't a monster. She really does like saving people, and she'll be sorry about every one who doesn't sign. The catch is what she doesn't say: her transport will log the fleet's position. How did she know where to be? The Honest Mistake, Halm's channel or pure patience. She won't say, and she'll ask one more question instead. The fleet's own rescue capacity is the Meridian's boats, a few ferries and whatever anyone else will send.
beats: The alarm, then the cutter. Pell is already asking for permission to launch. On the Landing's upper decks, people can see their breath.
Moor's offer, courteous, with datapads for everyone and boiled sweets for the children. Then the form with the captain's signature, in the same polite tone. "I'm sure there's a simple answer."
The first deck goes. Families hammer on the airlocks. People start signing. The captain can't stop them without guns, and can't really stop them with guns.

The call to the fleet: who'll come? The Sundial is warm and huge, and Steward Tull isn't answering. Everyone is listening to see what the others do. Then a small ferry turns out of formation: the Second Thursday. Then another.
The final count: who's saved, who signed, and who's still aboard when the last deck goes.
routes: Every ship takes ten: leadership to call the whole fleet in, and piloting for the small boats, a hundred little landings on a dying ship. It's the best thing the fleet will ever do, if enough of them come.
Keep the plant alive: engineering and void_ops with Marrow, running heat across an umbilical from the Meridian or refitting the coil they took. It buys hours and costs the next jump.
Face Moor: persuasion or commerce to change her terms, or intimidation and gunnery to warn off the cutter with one working cannon, while she politely notes the fact. She can be bargained with.
On the Landing: survival, medicine and athletics on the freezing decks. Get people moving, keep them together, carry the ones who can't walk. It's also a chance for the captain to be seen doing it.
checks: leadership:hard to turn forty-one frightened ships around
piloting:hard to land a boat on a dying ship's iced-up dock
engineering:very_hard to keep the heat plant limping along
void_ops:hard to rig an umbilical across open space
survival:moderate to keep a deck alive below freezing
gunnery:moderate to put a warning shot exactly where it needs to go
fights: desperate_refugee crush at the lifeboat hatch
customs_marine squad if Moor's people are fired on, or someone tries to seize her datapads
outcomes: Everyone off, nobody signed: the fleet did this by itself. It's the proudest moment since the Fall, and it burned a week of fuel. Moor thanks everyone, leaves a bag of sweets on the dock, and knows where the fleet is.
Some signed: a few hundred go with Moor, and they believe they made the right choice. They may be right. Their names are on a list at Bastion Nine, and the fleet is short a lot of people it liked.

All signed: the easy way, and nobody died. Moor thanks the captain on an open channel. Eleven hundred people are in Hegemony service by next week, and Speaker Halm would like to know what, exactly, is the argument against doing this for everyone.

The coil comes out: if Garrick Fenn gets the form, the next day's broadcast is one page long. The captain signed what they were given, and so has everyone. It's a fair question, and it doesn't stop being asked.
gm.rewards: Standing with the fleet, which may jump a long way up. Moor's card, with a single question written on the back. Deep gratitude from anyone who came off that ship.
